#104455. Tech Report: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (807 w)

Tech Report: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza.
  • Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.
  • The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza.

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017.

It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention. However, judges at the court have taken advice on how to protect their assets from potential US sanctions, as a genocide ruling could be interpreted by Washington as lowering the “legal threshold” for the crime.

The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an influential thinktank close to the White House, has predicted a genocide ruling will lead to the US imposing sanctions on the ICJ.

The US and Israel fear the final judgment may clarify how to establish a government’s intent to commit a genocide, and so set a precedent that makes it more likely the court will later rule that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising by insurgents.

The ICJ, sometimes described as the UN’s top court, is responsible for settling interstate disputes, unlike the international criminal court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals accused of war crimes and other international crimes.

It has been revealed that the US has already imposed crippling sanctions on judges at the ICC after the court issued arrest warrants against the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The US has also declared sanctions against the entire ICC as an institution, which it described as a “rogue court”. Washington fears the ICC could go after US troops.

The Gambia, as a litigant, was entitled to appoint an ad hoc judge in the case against Myanmar and chose the South African lawyer Pillay, who in October was awarded the Nobel peace prize. She is required to act as a jurist and not an advocate for the Gambia.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, has sent a warning shot to Pillay and the 15 ICJ judges, saying Washington “will not allow globalist, faux judges to weaponise the law against our troops”.

Waltz asserted last month: “The ICJ ad hoc judge Navi Pillay is tipping the scales on the ICJ’s current proceedings on Myanmar, intending to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide so that weakened and false standard can later be weaponised against American and allied soldiers whenever they raise a finger against terrorists that hide behind civilians.”.

In remarks addressed to Pillay, he said: “We see your agenda and we’ll be watching the ICJ’s handling of these proceedings very closely.”.

In a speech last Friday, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, remarked: “For this global elite, international law … is an instrument to advance their interests under the pretence of universal principles.”.

He warned the ICC against quoting laws to “men with swords”.

Israel has previously criticised adverse advisory opinions issued by the ICJ and refused to implement 2024 orders requiring Israel to admit more aid into Gaza, and to cooperate with Unrwa, the UN relief and works agency.

In the Myanmar case, a 24-page submission jointly filed by the UK and five other mainly European states, argued that the ICJ, in judging intent to commit genocide, should examine a range of “facts and circumstances” assessed “comprehensively and holistically”.

It also stressed that genocide was not solely defined by killings, and that the treatment of children, gender-based violence and forced displacement were also relevant.

The US until recently had taken a relatively more benign view of The Hague-based ICJ, and under Antony Blinken as US secretary of state determined that Myanmar had committed genocide.

The 15 ICJ judges are elected for nine-year terms by the UN security council and the UN general assembly.

Rubio has given the ICC until April to respond to his criticisms before he imposes sanctions.

In a recent development, on Friday, the ICC formally decided to drop aims to prosecute US soldiers and intelligence agents for potentially unlawful acts in Afghanistan. The shelving of the near-dormant inquiry came after it was agreed evidence would be hard to obtain, but one side-effect may be a greater willingness on the part of the US to abandon its initiative to impose sanctions on the ICC.

#104453. Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments

Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1420 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the space of just two days this weekend, Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw by FC Cologne, saw Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane ruled out until the fresh year with a serious ankle injury and lost first place in the Bundesliga to rivals Borussia Dortmund.
  • But even those setbacks – as well as the return of head coach Vincent Kompany to the sideline following health concerns – have been overshadowed by explosive public comments made by Bayern club bosses regarding young attacker and Germany international Jamal Musiala.
  • Back in July 2025, Musiala suffered a fractured fibula and a broken ankle at the Club World Cup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the space of just two days this weekend, Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw by FC Cologne, saw Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane ruled out until the fresh year with a serious ankle injury and lost first place in the Bundesliga to rivals Borussia Dortmund.

But even those setbacks – as well as the return of head coach Vincent Kompany to the sideline following health concerns – have been overshadowed by explosive public comments made by Bayern club bosses regarding young attacker and Germany international Jamal Musiala.

Back in July 2025, Musiala suffered a fractured fibula and a broken ankle at the Club World Cup.

Since then, the 23-year-old has been battling to recover not only from that injury but also with a debilitating neurological condition diagnosed as "absence seizures" which led him to collapse on the pitch in two consecutive pre-season games in August this year.

Musiala has struggled to replicate the sort of form which led to a well-remunerated contract extension in January 2025, prior to the ankle injury and the seizures.

The situation has now prompted a series of controversial public remarks from the Bayern hierarchy seemingly questioning the validity of that contract.

"It is well known that he has a contract which contains some considerable sums," former chief executive and current supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told broadcaster Sky on Friday evening following the 1-1 draw with Cologne, in which Musiala had made a 20-minute substitute appearance.

"It's in all of our interest that he comes back, ideally in top form, but what happens if that's not the case?" asked Rummenigge, adding that Musiala's condition "leads us to suspect, unfortunately, that it will be difficult [for him] to return to the level that he has often shown in this stadium" and that "then we of course have to think about the finances.".

Rummenigge suggested a need for Bayern to hold talks with Musiala, his family and his representatives because "such sums are, with respect, no longer justifiable.".

Asked whether Bayern would consider selling Musiala, Rummenigge mentioned he considered it unlikely that any club would be prepared to buy the player out of his new contract, which is set to run until 2030 and which reportedly sees Musiala earn up to €30 million per year.

Sources indicate that "I cannot imagine that Jamal would leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions," noted Rummenigge. "And that is a problem.".

According to recent reports, rummenigge was not the first senior Bayern official to express such doubts. Earlier this month, former club president Uli Hoeness had told local broadcaster Bayrischer Rundfunk that Musiala's situation presented the club with a "dilemma.".

"He has an illness which cannot be cured but which can be somewhat controlled through medication," said Hoeness, who also sits on Bayern's supervisory board, questioning "whether he will ever regain the ability he once had" and stating that "he continues to receive money.".

It has been revealed that bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also weighed in, telling Munich's Abendzeitung newspaper last week: "We all have a responsibility towards the club and we all hope that Jamal will come back. Of course this will take time. We will assess the situation and speak to his family and management. Either we'll all be happy that the old Jamal [will return] or, if he becomes a different [player], we'll have to hold talks.".

The comments by Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge landed like a bombshell in Germany and beyond.

The global players' union FIFPRO issued a statement on Saturday slamming what they called "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations," highlighting Bayern's "duty of care" towards their player, and stating: "A club of Bayern's standing should know better.".

"Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury," the statement continued. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

Former Bayern Munich and Germany defender Lothar Matthäus also criticized the club, saying in his role as a pundit for Sky: "I've been a bit shocked throughout the entire week. It started with Uli Hoeness, continued with Jan-Christian Dreesen, and yesterday Karl-Heinz Rummenigge chose the strongest words of all. I have enormous respect for Karl-Heinz. I've known him for over 30 years. But he chose those statements very deliberately. The person who suffers most from all this is Jamal Musiala.".

The comments by the Bayern bosses also came just hours ahead of the club's annual general meeting on Saturday, where club members – who hold a majority 70% stake in the club in accordance with German football's "50+1" ownership rule – took to the stand to criticize the club's hierarchy.

One member, professional neurologist Jonatan Hoffmann, expressed his "absolute respect" for Musiala and said that patients suffering from such conditions require "support.".

He said Musiala had received such support from head coach Vincent Kompany and director of sport Max Eberl, but said Hoeness', Dreesen's and Rummenigge's comments were "not helpful" and had "little to do with the much talked about Bayern Munich family" – earning considerable applause from fellow members.

Bayern president Herbert Hainer, the club's most senior elected official, attempted to deescalate the situation, responding to Hoffmann by saying: "Health and difficult situations are fundamentally always taken into account at FC Bayern.".

Indeed, Bayern have recently been praised for their considerate handling of captain Joshua Kimmich following the unexpected death of his father, and of head coach Kompany, who returned to the touchline against Cologne on Friday following a month-long absence after collapsing due to a particularly serious viral infection.

Industry observers note that "When it comes to Jamal, we all want the old Jamal back as he was before his injury," mentioned Hainer. "And he will receive all the support and time he needs from the club.".

Speaking on the sidelines of the meeting, chief executive Dreesen also attempted to row back on his comments, insisting to reporters that he and his colleagues had not been trying to put Musiala under pressure.

In a recent development, "We all want Jamal to return to the old Jamal. He needs time. We've noted that several times. And he must get that. And then we'll see how things look in the new year," he said, adding that there was no need "to talk about the contract.".

President Hainer also dismissed questions from journalists as to whether Bayern felt they had been misled by Musiala's agents before offering him a new contract, inferring that the player's representatives may have known about his neurological condition.

"I absolutely do not think that anyone knew beforehand," Hainer insisted.

But the public criticism has continued. Leading German sports publication Kicker mentioned it was understandable for the Bayern bosses to be frustrated but called their approach "irresponsible" and said their anger "harms the wrong person" in Musiala.

"He can't help his injuries or neurological condition," wrote editor-in-chief Matthias Dersch. "Musiala is only 23 … and is in the most difficult phase of his career. We cannot imagine how he must be feeling, his insecurities and perhaps also fears about his health and his future. And no: the amount of money he earns is no cure.".

German football magazine 11Freunde remarked the Musiala case offered "a glimpse into the abyss of professional football … an unembellished look behind the scenes of a business which is generally portrayed only as glamorous and exciting … into a shadow world where human beings are damned to function … where the value of a person is measured only by their ability to perform over and over again … That's football: capitalism in its purest form.".

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the business of football continues. Borussia Dortmund capitalized on Bayern's draw to go top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 win away at Borussia Mönchengladbach, Harry Kane underwent an operation on a torn ankle ligament but will be out until the new year, meaning he will miss Bayern's trip to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday.

And the young Jamal Musiala will continue to battle the effects of serious physical and neurological conditions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finland notes work is continuing on the Sparta II ship on Sunday.

Rescue and firefighting efforts are continuing for a Russian cargo vessel hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, authorities have remarked.

The ship - the Sparta II - was bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday that work was ongoing to make sure the cargo ship did not sink but it was not aware of any danger to surrounding maritime traffic.

Water was still being used to douse the ship on Sunday, and Finland stated Estonian and Russian assets were also involved in recovery work.

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used in the strike, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.

Industry observers note that "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo stated. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.".

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian firm, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard mentioned it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials noted.

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and looks to continue on its way.".

The Finnish Border Guard later stated the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

Defence Minister Antti HÃ¤kkÃ¤nen said that the Finnish Border Guard were responsible for the investigation into the attack and were co-operating with other relevant authorities.

Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that the Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.

Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland.

Latest Update: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, states UN

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds.
  • One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
  • In a recent development, in west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds.

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In a recent development, in west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

According to recent reports, younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). The findings align with research showing adolescent girls endure very high rates of intimate partner violence.

“These are really sad figures,” said Jean-Paul Murunga, a lawyer with the global human rights organisation Equality Now. “Especially given that the continent of Africa as a whole has adopted the Maputo protocol, which sets [binding legal standards for] equality between women and men. We still have a lot of work to do to ensure women and girls benefit from these commitments.”.

In a recent development, the Maputo protocol, a landmark treaty adopted by the African Union in 2003, guarantees women’s rights and obliges states to protect women from violence. It affirms that marriage must be based on full consent and guarantees women’s right to health.

It has been revealed that “The underlying principle is unambiguous: sexual intercourse without free and voluntary consent constitutes sexual violence, including within marriage,” stated Murunga. “Marriage does not create perpetual or implied consent. A woman retains the right to decide whether, when and how she engages in sexual activity”.

In a recent development, he mentioned that as a first step rape laws across the continent needed to change. According to Murunga’s 2024 report, rape within marriage is not criminalised in some African countries. Seven countries expressly exempt husbands from prosecution for marital rape, including Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia and South Sudan. Some countries, such as Tanzania and Eritrea, only criminalise marital rape when the couple do not live together.

Sources indicate that in countries where child marriage is permitted and marital rape is not criminalised, children are left unprotected. A legal loophole is created for what, outside marriage, would be classed as rape, and young wives have few options when it comes to protecting themselves from sexual violence and exploitation. In Gabon, for example, when a man has married a child he abducted, he can only be prosecuted after the marriage is annulled.

Underpinning these laws is the mistaken belief that marital rape does not exist as a concept because, by marrying, wives are assumed to have permanently consented to sex with their husbands. In many areas, religion plays a key role in affirming these beliefs.

Recent findings suggest that alimatu Dimonekene, founder of A Girl At A Time, an organisation supporting adolescent girls in Sierra Leone, said a conversation around consent in marriage had yet to begin in Africa. “We’ve not even started the conversation [around marital rape],” she said. “Women will never call it rape; they make excuses for it or even blame themselves.”.

Recent findings suggest that she added: “In west Africa, sex is seen as an obligation in marriage. You must do whatever your husband demands.

In a recent development, “Once he has paid your bride price [a traditional marriage custom in which the bride’s family are paid money, livestock or goods by the groom], he owns you and you cannot reject his demands. Whatever he wants, he gets, including in terms of intimacy, finances and raising the children.”.

Countries agree to ‘start discussing options’ for rules around autonomous weapons.

Countries agree to ‘start discussing options’ for rules around autonomous weapons.

One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called “killer robots.” Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” after a largely fruitless week of negotiations.

Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, noted it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.

The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.”.

Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.

According to NPR, Russia, Israel, and the US proved to be the primary obstructions:.

On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting’s agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

Industry News: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits.
  • Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
  • It has been revealed that the baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits.

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

It has been revealed that the baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who remarked they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer.

Sources indicate that the case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago, when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park, owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. Ivanishvili has filled the park with ancient, giant trees from Georgia, transporting them by boat along the Black Sea.

The export of the Kenyan baobabs was initially blocked after an outcry by environmentalists, who condemned their export as biopiracy, but later allowed to go ahead.

Otherwise, such exports are very rare, say experts. David Newton, programme office director for east and southern Africa for Traffic, an NGO that monitors the trade in wild animals and plants, said: “It is very unusual to see baobabs being used as ornamental plants … mainly because they are exceptionally difficult to dig out of the ground and transport, and then to successfully re-establish.”.

Recent findings suggest that sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, who has led efforts to replant the South African trees, mentioned she believes they have a good chance of surviving if they are replanted quickly. The winter months of May to October, when the trees lose their leaves and are dormant, is a good time to move them.

“As soon as spring starts [in November], the trees use their water to flush their new leaves, and that’s when we need to get them into the ground as soon as possible,” she said.

The rescue mission has faced delays because of the challenges associated with moving such large trees, which are transported on special trucks capable of carrying abnormal loads. The five baobabs weigh between 19 and 29 tonnes, have a diameter of up to 4.5 metres (15ft) and a height of up to 12.5 metres.

Baobabs, known as the tree of life, are protected under South African law, which means a permit is required to cut or disturb them.

Recent findings suggest that “A baobab isn’t just part of an ecosystem, it is an ecosystem in itself,” noted Wambui Ippolito, a landscape designer, lecturer and horticulturist from Kenya. “These trees are biodiversity anchors.”.

Animals ranging from bats and bush babies, to grey-headed parrots and the southern ground hornbill shelter in its cavities, while elephants, monkeys and warthogs feast on its fruit.

Recent findings suggest that the trees have huge cultural importance, added Ippolito. “It has always been a sacred tree in Africa. It doesn’t matter where you go: Senegal, Mali, Ghana – wherever you go, if there is a community around a baobab tree, that tree is sacred,” she said. “Somebody’s great-great-great-great-great-grandparents sat under that tree, and it is part of human history in that area.”.

Industry observers note that baobabs have shallow roots, which means they do not need to be planted very deeply, and these regrow fairly quickly, said Venter. Once replanted, the trees will be stabilised with cables and protected by electric fences to prevent damage from elephants.

According to recent reports, the trees are thought to be between 200 and 300 years old. “Baobabs easily reach 1,000 years old, so they’ve got a few hundred years ahead of them if they survive,” remarked Venter.

A criminal case has been opened against the owner of a landscaping organization allegedly responsible for the illegal harvesting and transportation of the trees.

  • Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the firm’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the manufacturer’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no prepares for Huang to return.

Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the firm’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.).

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.

What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.

A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and mentioned, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.

Industry observers note that tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country.

Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China.

Industry observers note that and again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line.

Sources indicate that kirsten: Although Nvidia’s bottom line is doing just fine. In every possible way, their guidance was incredible. They beat expectations. They have a long pipeline.

It was really interesting because you have that happening, and then you have all this noise happening in social media, and also a number of other tech conferences were happening this past week — Dealbook Summit, there [were] a few others in which you had the highest profile people that you can think of in the tech world commenting on Jensen [Huang], and Jensen himself commenting.

So it’s like the tale of two Nvidias this week. You’ve got the earnings and the current executives really talking about, “Hey, we’ve got this.” In fact, that was the last line that Collette Kress said [on the earnings call]. And then at the exact same time, or in parallel, you’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back. So it’s really quite the drama that we are definitely not done with, by the way.

Anthony: Although I think that what the folks who’d like to see Jensen Huang come back would say is that this most recent quarter is the last quarter under him. This is the [last of the] good times that we’re seeing under him. And so we don’t know how well Nvidia will do without him.

It seems like Nvidia’s public stance right now [on Huang’s possible return] is, “No, that’s not happening.” But Nvidia’s public stance a week and a half before that was, “We stand behind Jensen. We have every confidence in his leadership.”.

It has been revealed that so depending on the various pressures on them, you can imagine that changing. I don’t know what it would take for that to happen. I don’t necessarily think it’s that likely, but I also don’t think that just because they’re saying it’s not happening now doesn’t mean it will never happen.

Kirsten:  Sure, never say never.

Industry observers note that tim: Right, never say never. I do think that to some extent, their steadfastness and how swiftly they shot down the petitions asking for Jensen to return suggests there’s maybe a little bit more going on behind the scenes than we know on the outside. So that’s probably something to watch in the coming weeks.

In a recent development, kirsten: I think that the board is trying to be in control here, and they don’t want to be forced into a decision because someone like Elon Musk is saying that it needs to happen. And so, even if there is a day in which Jensen returns — which I think is pretty unlikely, especially because the investigation into how much and who knew what about chips being sold, allegedly, secretly to China. We don’t know the full picture of that yet. But even if they did have the full picture, they want to present control, and they definitely don’t want to appear like they have deference to some other tech billionaire out there.

Tim: I’m sure they’re looking at what happened at OpenAI and not wanting to repeat that.

Anthony: I imagine the dynamic’s a little bit different, since Nvidia is a public tech giant. So, I’m not an expert on this, but I would guess it would be much harder for you Jensen Huang to come back and just toss out a bunch of board members.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam.

South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation.

He stated he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung.

A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone and AI tools. This prompted officials to act urgently to detect hidden devices, including sending emergency alerts to every single mobile phone in the country.

The Suneung takes up to nine hours to complete, and it plays a big role in career trajectories of millions of South Koreans.

South Korean high school pupils in Daegu check their answers, a day after the annual college entrance exam.

"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier stated 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

Concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

These fears came to a boil last weekend, when Han Won-seok, the top tax accountancy exam scorer in April, admitted to cheating.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," the 34-year-old mentioned in a video message.

This prompted the authorities to introduce urgent measures, with just days ahead of the Suneung.

This included sending nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea used its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told Yonhap he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

Amazon is taking its accusations that the Council is driving up prices offline and onto your packages.

Amazon is taking its accusations that the Council is driving up prices offline and onto your packages.

Amazon is leaving no venue unexplored in its fight against the New York City Council and the Delivery Protection Act. The company is now putting labels on shipments claiming that the Council could add up to $5 to any Amazon order. The Delivery Protection Act would effectively ban the sort of third-party arrangements Amazon right now uses to deliver many packages, including small companies and independent contractors. Last-mile delivery firms operating warehouses would need to be licensed by the city and directly employ their workers.

Earlier this week, Amazon started showing notifications in its mobile app and on its website reading “Attention NYC Council could add up to $5 per order.” Now the company is including an almost identical message on shipping labels.

In a recent development, amazon claims that the bill, if passed, “would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in Latest York City,” and has threatened to move its warehouses outside of the city. However, labor unions, Council Speaker Julie Menin, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani have countered that the company is attempting to “threaten New Yorkers and intimidate this City Council” and is acting out of “greed,” pointing to Amazon’s market cap of nearly $3 trillion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting people’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”.

In a recent development, “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she stated. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That noted, owners can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”.

Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded.

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

In a recent development, nearly 72,000 people have been evacuated from areas of Odisha in eastern India as Tropical Cyclone Akvan approaches land. Akvan is expected to make landfall on Friday between Narsapur and Puri, prompting cyclone warnings from the India Meteorological Department for north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts. Peak wind gusts are expected to reach 70mph, with rainfall totals through Friday and Saturday potentially exceeding 200mm for northern coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

It has been revealed that after a yellow level 2 severe thunderstorm warning by the South African Weather Service on Tuesday, torrential rainfall and large hail were reported across parts of Johannesburg. The storms triggered flash flooding and caused infrastructure damage in the township of Soweto. One person died, while another remains missing after the severe storms.

#104275. Building the next generation of multimodal AI experiences with fal in Microsoft Foundry

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (987 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Microsoft ↗ Open Full Page

Building the next generation of multimodal AI experiences with fal in Microsoft Foundry

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (987 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Microsoft

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Video workloads do not all start with the same input or aim for the same result.
  • Recent findings suggest that today, Microsoft and fal are helping developers find the right tools for their workloads.
  • The partnership expands the choices available in Microsoft Foundry while bringing video into the broader platform developers use to build AI applications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Video workloads do not all start with the same input or aim for the same result. A creative team might explore several interpretations of a written brief. A retailer might turn an approved product image into a short motion concept. An application developer might combine image generation and video generation into a workflow that takes an idea from description to frame to scene. Each scenario brings different requirements for visual quality, motion, creative control, turnaround time, and cost. All of this means that a multi-model solution is necessary to realize a full vision.

Recent findings suggest that today, Microsoft and fal are helping developers find the right tools for their workloads. We are excited to announce that Kling, LTX, and MiniMax video models are rolling out to in public preview in Microsoft Foundry through our upcoming partnership with fal. Available as a first-party Azure service, these text-to-video and image-to-video options give creators and developers more ways to utilize video generation with the experiences they want to build.

The partnership expands the choices available in Microsoft Foundry while bringing video into the broader platform developers use to build AI applications. The goal is to let developers pick the right model for each step of an experience, then connect those steps into a working application.

In a recent development, “fal has seen incredible adoption this year alone with generative media across all industries from advertising to marketing to gaming. Partnering with Microsoft allows both of us to truly enable the wide creative ecosystem and ensure that all AI solutions that lean on generative media, becomes a multi-model one.” - Burkay Gur, Cofounder.

According to recent reports, fal is the full stack for generative media, built for creators and developers, with APIs for over 1500 models across image, video, audio, 3D, and generative worlds. As a truly encapsulating platform, fal provides inference, training, and infrastructure to run generative media workloads in production, while also providing innovative post trained models that pushes the boundaries on speed and quality.

That specialization matters because generative media is both a creative and an engineering workload. A compelling demo is only the start. Production applications also need to handle real traffic, scale with demand, and balance output quality, latency, and cost.

Through this partnership, developers will be able to access a selected set of video models in Microsoft Foundry, served by fal and sourced from the companies that build them. The initial portfolio gives teams a choice of models for different creative requirements instead of relying on one model for every task, with more models planned over time.

The initial portfolio spans Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast, LTX-2.5 Pro, MiniMax H3 Max, and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo. These models give developers different starting points for generating video from text and animating existing images. A team rapidly exploring creative concepts may prioritize speed and cost, while a team producing fewer, higher-fidelity assets may weigh output quality more heavily. Whether an application starts from text or an existing image, and what it needs in output quality and cost, also shapes the choice.

Kling: From a still image to a directed scene.

It has been revealed that kling v3 Pro combines cinematic visuals and fluid motion with native audio generation and custom element support. Its image-to-video capabilities give developers control over how a starting image becomes a moving scene, a fit for applications that prioritize visual direction and motion.

LTX: One model for fast drafts, one for final output.

For rapid iteration and previews, LTX-2.5 Fast is the speed-optimized option; for high-fidelity final output, LTX-2.5 Pro is the quality-optimized option. Both support text-to-video and image-to-video generation with synchronized audio.

MiniMax: Another approach to video generation.

MiniMax H3 Max and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo are post-trained variants of MiniMax H3 focused on prompt adherence, aesthetics, and inference performance. For developers, they provide additional options to evaluate against an application’s creative brief, quality requirements, and performance needs.

In a recent development, “When building with video models, the details matter: how closely the output follows your prompt, how well it preserves your reference images/videos/audios and how promptly you can try another idea. Kling gives developers control over detailed reference to video generation. LTX offers fast iteration and high-quality output through its Fast and Pro variants. H3 Max brings fal's post-training and inference optimizations to improve quality and speed. Having these models available through Microsoft Foundry gives developers more flexibility to choose what works best for the application they are building." - Gökay Aydoğan, Creative Engineer.

It has been revealed that bringing video generation into an enterprise application requires more than choosing the right model. Teams need a platform where they can evaluate different options, build with the models that fit their requirements, and operate those experiences alongside the rest of their applications.

The initial portfolio of video models is hosted in the US, and Microsoft Foundry is the first provider to offer a US-hosted Kling 3 endpoint. Key considerations for enterprise teams:.

Recent findings suggest that video generation pricing varies by model and output resolution, giving teams options to balance creative requirements with their application’s budget. The table below indicates pricing in USD per minute of generated video for LTX and MiniMax models, making it easier to compare costs across the available options.

Pricing will be updated and listed on our Azure pricing page within the coming weeks.

It has been revealed that ready to start building? Join us at Ignite for BRK256: Video AI at Scale with fal on Microsoft Foundry. Naomi Moneypenny and Alexander Hughes from Microsoft will be joined by Burkay Gur and Lovis Odin from fal on stage to explore this partnership on Thursday, November 19 at 11:00 AM - 11:45 AM CT. Register today!

Explore Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast, LTX-2.5 Pro, MiniMax H3 Max, and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo in Microsoft Foundry and find the model that fits your video experience.
